links.comparator_used: Same CADe (CAD EYE) run under white-light imaging (WLI) within the same patients
links.outcome: Number of false-positive CADe detection boxes per case, and positive predictive value
links.effect: False-positive boxes per case 3.48 (2.55) with LCI vs 7.70 (4.81) with WLI; mean difference 4.32, P < .001. Total boxes 204 (LCI) vs 801 (WLI) with 5 true cancers in each; PPV 2.45% vs 0.62%. Lower with LCI in all H. pylori status groups.
links.tradeoff: Both modes still produced false positives (average 6.2 per case overall). Each patient was observed with both modes; no added time or cost was reported for LCI.
links.quote: Paired t test analysis demonstrated that the number of false-positive detection boxes was significantly lower with LCI than with WLI (mean difference: 4.32; 95% CI, 5.01 to −3.64; P < .001).

links.outcome: Gastric cancer detection rate during EGD with real-time CADe detection boxes
links.effect: GC detection 4.8% (5/105) with CADe vs 1.8% (11/600) in unmatched controls (P = .07); vs 0.95% (1/105) in matched controls (P = .098). Biopsy rate 22.9% vs 16.2% (NS); exam time 12.1 vs 11.1 min (NS).
links.tradeoff: High false-positive rate: an average of 6.2 detection boxes per case at non-tumor sites. Biopsy rate and exam time were slightly higher with CADe, but not significantly. Possible downstream workload was noted as a concern.
links.quote: The GC detection rate in the CADe group was slightly higher than in the control group (difference, 3.0%; 95% CI, 0.3%-6.3%), although the difference was not statistically significant ( P = .07).

design_hint: imaging mode selection (linked-color vs white-light imaging) for CADe use
